newsitem.title: USA: VLSI Technology unveils chipmaking roadmap.
newsitem.headline: VLSI Technology unveils chipmaking roadmap.

text.p: VLSI Technology Inc. on Monday unveiled its semiconductor product plans for the next few years based on advanced chipmaking technologies.
VLSI -- a maker of custom chips for consumer electronics, telecommunication equipment and computers -- said it will use microscopic transistors just 0.25 and 0.20 micron wide.

With transistors that small, VLSI can pack more computing horsepower on a single chip, which speeds up calculations and reduces power consumption, said Jeff Hendy, VLSI vice president of global market services.
Currently, most of the industry makes transistors at 0.5 or 0.35 microns.
The new chips from VLSI, based in San Jose, Calif., will appear in devices such as cellular phones, video game consoles, computer networking gear and consumer electronics, Hendy said.
Production of the new chips will begin in the fourth quarter, the company said.
